headline: Trees cut over the holiday. The judge: "unamused."
summary: Judge Ana Reyes on Monday halted tree-cutting at the East Potomac Golf Course in Washington for 24 hours. The course is part of President Trump's plan to remake the city. Crews felled the trees over the holiday weekend while a lawsuit to stop the work sat in her court. She wants an Interior official in court Tuesday to explain the rush.

cover_question.q: Why cut on a holiday weekend?

cover_answer: Nobody has said. The judge wants that answer Tuesday.
table_question: Is it cheating to go ahead while the referee is still deciding?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: In Washington, workers cut down a lot of trees at a golf course over the long weekend, trees taller than a house, while a judge was still deciding whether they were allowed to. On Monday the judge said stop for a day and come explain. A judge is like the teacher who decides what is fair when two kids disagree. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Cutting while the teacher decides. A six-year-old knows that one.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and a lawsuit is not, so the script gives them the trees, taller than a house, and the teacher who decides what is fair. Your calm is what tells them this is a story about fairness. Expect "will they get in trouble?" The judge wants an explanation Tuesday. That is the trouble so far.

8-12.script: A group sued to stop the rebuild of a Washington golf course. Judge Ana Reyes was still deciding when crews cut the trees over the holiday weekend. She halted the work Monday and summoned the man who rushed it. It is running the play with the referee's arm up.
8-12.why: Lawsuit, weekend, chainsaws, halt. A whistle they know.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules, so the script runs the chain: a lawsuit waiting on a judge, trees cut while she was still deciding, a halt, a summons. Running the play while the referee's arm is up is a call they have argued. Expect "can they put the trees back?" No. The order stops the next cut, not the last one.

13-17.script: Judge Reyes said she gave the government "every single benefit of the doubt" and it cut the trees anyway, over a holiday, with a lawsuit pending. If you can't undo it, what is a court order worth? Second: she had refused to halt the work before. Was her trust used, or did she wait too long?
13-17.why: A judge who trusted, then a chainsaw. Then her own part in it.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the government ignored what a judge made plain, and the judge had kept declining to stop it. The script asks what an order is worth once the trees are down, and makes them argue against a judge they may side with. Expect "what happens now?" A hearing Tuesday. The order can stretch to 14 days.

5-7.q: Why did they cut the trees down?
5-7.a: The government is rebuilding the golf course. The judge wants to know why it couldn't wait.

8-12.q: Why cut trees on a holiday?
8-12.a: Nobody has said. The judge summoned the man who rushed it.

8-12.q: Can the judge make them put the trees back?
8-12.a: No. She can stop more cutting and make officials explain why.

13-17.q: Why cut on a holiday weekend?
13-17.a: Nobody has said. She wants Greg Wischer of Interior in court Tuesday.

13-17.q: What can a judge actually do about it?
13-17.a: Stop the next cut, a day now and up to 14, and make officials explain.
